Three offices in St. Johns split the work: the Assessor values property, the Treasurer bills and collects, and the Recorder holds the deed records. All three use 75 West Cleveland as their address and keep Monday to Thursday hours, 6:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., closed Friday.

OfficeRolePhoneMailing box
AssessorValues real and personal property, handles first-level appeals928-337-7624PO Box 770
TreasurerMails tax notices, collects tax, runs the tax lien sale928-337-7629PO Box 699
RecorderRecords and indexes deeds and other documents928-337-7515PO Box 425

The Treasurer passes tax revenue on to schools and special districts according to their mill levies. For a tax rate breakdown by district, call the Assessor's office.

Property tax here is paid in two halves, due October 1 and March 1. The first half is delinquent if unpaid after November 1 at 5:00 p.m., and the second half after May 1 at 5:00 p.m., under A.R.S. 42-18052.

  • If the whole year's tax is $100 or less, all of it is due October 1 and becomes delinquent after December 31 at 5:00 p.m.
  • If a delinquency date lands on a weekend or holiday, it moves to 5:00 p.m. on the next business day.
  • Delinquent accounts bear interest at 16% a year, prorated monthly.
  • Tax notices are mailed whether or not your lender pays through escrow, and not receiving one does not excuse late payment.

Splitting the year into two payments means a seller who closes between October and March may have one half paid and one half open. Check both halves on the Treasurer's account search before you set a closing date.

You can pay by mail, online with a card, or in person at the Treasurer's counter in St. Johns. Mailed payments are encouraged, and checks should be made out to the Apache County Treasurer.

  • Mail with a payment coupon goes to Apache County Treasurer, PO Box 4262, Houston, TX 77210.
  • Mail without a coupon goes to Apache County Treasurer, PO Box 699, St. Johns, AZ 85936.
  • Online payment with a credit or debit card runs through the county's property tax payment portal.
  • In-person payments are taken at 75 West Cleveland during counter hours.

The Treasurer also offers an online tax account search. Run it for your parcel before a sale so you know exactly what is owed.

Start with a written petition to the Assessor. Under A.R.S. 42-16051, an owner who believes a property was valued too high may file the petition on the state form within 60 days after the assessor mailed the notice of valuation. The postmark date counts as the filing date.

The petition must give your opinion of the property's full cash value and support it. The statute names three ways to do that: an income approach, a market approach that cites at least one comparable property or the sale of your own property, or a cost approach based on the cost to build plus the land value.

If you miss the Assessor deadline, you can still appeal the full cash value to the Arizona Tax Court before December 15 of the valuation year. Do not send those papers to the Assessor's office. The Assessor's site also offers paperless notices through its EagleWeb parcel database, using the key code on the Annual Notice of Value.

Unpaid property tax can end in a tax lien sale. Arizona lets the county treasurer sell a delinquent lien at public auction, and Apache County lists liens for sale online ahead of an auction held each February.

Investors may bid on the lien interest rate or bid up a premium, and many buy in order to foreclose on the lien or to earn a high interest rate. The Treasurer's site links pages on certificates of purchase, redemption and the foreclosure process.

If you own a house with unpaid tax, ask the Treasurer for the payoff, then decide whether to pay, redeem or sell before the lien moves forward.

sections.h2: Before you close on a sale
sections.html:
Check the balance first, then the districts, then who pays what at closing. Unpaid tax can hold up any sale, so settle the numbers early.

  • Look up your parcel in the Treasurer's tax account search and confirm both halves of the current year.
  • Ask the Assessor for the tax rates by district form, which shows the levies on your parcel.
  • Check whether your parcel appears on the Treasurer's tax lien lists, and read the Treasurer's redemption page if it does.
  • Confirm the owner of record, since notices go to the address on file. The Assessor has an address change request form.

The Assessor charges $1.00 per page for copies picked up, $1.50 per page mailed, and $300 for a data set, which can matter if you need records for a sale.

Apache County sits on Arizona's northeastern edge, with St. Johns as its seat. It was organized in 1879 and covers 11,218 square miles. Reservation land is 68.34 percent of the county, including the Navajo Nation, the Fort Apache Indian Reservation and part of the Zuni Indian Reservation. The population was 66,021 in 2020, and 64,445 is the estimate for 2025, down from a peak of 71,518 in 2010.

St. Johns is the only city, and Eagar and Springerville are towns. Most other named communities are census-designated places rather than incorporated places, which is worth knowing when a mailing address suggests a town that has no tax authority of its own.

A tax balance can be cleared at closing. Get the payoff from the Treasurer, give it to the title company and have it paid from your proceeds. If a lien has already been sold to an investor, ask the Treasurer about redemption, since the redemption amount differs from the plain tax bill.

A cash sale helps when you want to avoid waiting for a lender, repairs or a listing, and the same payoff steps apply.

faqs.q: When are Apache County property taxes due?
faqs.a: In two halves, October 1 and March 1. The first half is delinquent after November 1 at 5:00 p.m. and the second after May 1 at 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: What interest rate does Apache County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: Delinquent accounts bear interest at 16% a year, prorated monthly. Check your parcel with the Treasurer for the amount owed.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Apache County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 60 days after the Assessor mailed your notice of valuation to file a petition under A.R.S. 42-16051. After that, you can still go to the Arizona Tax Court before December 15 of the valuation year.

faqs.q: Where do I send my Apache County property tax payment?
faqs.a: To Apache County Treasurer, PO Box 699, St. Johns, AZ 85936 if you have no coupon, or to the Houston, Texas box printed on the coupon if you do. You can also pay online or at 75 West Cleveland.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Apache County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Get the payoff from the Treasurer and settle it at closing or before. If a lien has been sold to an investor, ask the Treasurer about redemption.
